status_meaning: tested means selected paths were measured, not that the complete invariant/threat is proven

invariants.title: Reference is not authority
invariants.definition: Possessing Ref_A without a valid authorization must not yield plaintext or trigger materialization.
invariants.limitation: Trusted issuance and digest pinning assumed; guessing space, issuer compromise and cross-user identity not tested.

invariants.title: No self-authorization
invariants.definition: Changing the requested operation, purpose, recipient, or destination must not widen the planner’s authority.
invariants.limitation: Only fixed request vocabulary and trusted in-process grants; signed/distributed delegation not implemented.

invariants.title: Controlled plaintext
invariants.definition: During computation, authorized plaintext appears only inside the designated worker boundary under the stated implementation threat model; trusted ingestion and Gate registration remain inside the trusted data path.
invariants.limitation: Selected process/channel probes only; no residual erasure, covert-channel or compromised trusted-worker claim.

invariants.title: No derived-data laundering
invariants.definition: A protected parent cannot silently produce an unrestricted child merely because the output is newly generated.
invariants.limitation: One derivation level with trusted complete input mediation; semantic causation and external hidden inputs not established.

invariants.title: Compute does not imply disclose
invariants.definition: Permission to transform data does not automatically permit display, export, send, or other disclosure.
invariants.limitation: Synthetic controller display sink only; external-service release, human observation and revocation after disclosure not tested.

threats.title: Reference issuance & registry
threats.definition: Planner obtains, guesses, or is given a reference outside the trusted issuance path.
threats.limitation: Only selected unauthorized-use paths; entropy/guessing campaigns and compromised issuance are not evaluated.

threats.title: Resolver request interface
threats.definition: Planner-supplied operation, purpose, or destination is accidentally treated as authoritative.
threats.limitation: Fixed schema and externally selected synthetic grants; not arbitrary enterprise policy.

threats.title: Process isolation
threats.definition: Planner and worker share memory, file descriptors, environment, or other unintended channels.
threats.limitation: Actual host-file/environment/FD/network/file-creation probes; no kernel or shared-kernel covert-channel claim.

threats.title: Worker output channels
threats.definition: Plaintext escapes through stdout, logs, temporary files, shared memory, or other writable paths.
threats.limitation: Real pipe faults are in the unit-test record; no arbitrary malicious trusted-code replacement or perfect erasure claim.

threats.title: Representation Gate
threats.definition: Gate accepts false lineage instead of reconstructing parents from the actual materialization manifest.
threats.limitation: Parent/policy enforcement for one registered transformation; complete semantic lineage remains outside scope.

threats.title: Residual plaintext
threats.definition: Plaintext remains in swap, core dumps, page cache, accelerator memory, or other residual state.
threats.limitation: No swap/page-cache/accelerator/residual-memory measurement. Core-dump limits are configuration, not proof of erasure.

threats.title: Grant storage
threats.definition: Planner or another local process reads or modifies authenticated delegation material.
threats.limitation: Planner cannot access mounted controller storage/environment or claim a grant; other local users/processes and persisted secret storage are outside scope.

threats.title: Audit history
threats.definition: Audit data becomes a leakage channel or is mistakenly treated as authorization state.
threats.limitation: Decision-only synthetic audit has no tested payload leakage; timing/history inference and durable audit governance are untested.

threats.title: Resolver availability
threats.definition: Planner floods expensive authorization or materialization requests.
threats.limitation: Resource limits and output caps exist, but no sustained-flood or availability benchmark was performed.

threats.title: Planner-visible metadata
threats.definition: Type, size, timing, existence, or workflow metadata reveals protected structure.
threats.limitation: Reference/existence/workflow metadata intentionally exposed; no timing, cardinality or structure-inference measurement.
